editorial:
Imagine watching a movie inside a movie, and then watching a play based on that same movie. That is exactly what you get here. You follow three girls from the Nogizaka46 pop group who are trying their best to act in a sci-fi story about a psychic club. The vibe is really quirky and lighthearted. You get to see the funny behind-the-scenes moments where the girls struggle with their lines, mixed with the actual plot about a classmate who is actually an alien from outer space. It feels like a cozy, weird experiment that keeps you guessing about which version of the story is the real one.

What really works is how the movie switches between the documentary style and the scripted drama. The acting is cute and charming, even if the idols aren't professional actors. Some parts might feel a bit slow because of the jumping timelines, but the payoff is worth it. If you like Japanese cinema or just want something different, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing how the different versions of the story blend together. You find out that the alien plot was just part of the script, but the real heart of the film is the friendship between the three girls. After the stage play ends, the lines between acting and reality blur one last time. It ends on a sweet note, showing that the experience of making the film changed them for the better.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Japanese idol culture or meta-storytelling.
